title: serving-runtime-weekly-update-kernel-kv-batching-2026-06-17
content:
Serving Runtime Weekly Update -- kernel / KV cache / batching
Date: 2026-06-17
Owner: Priya Shah
Attendees: Priya, Ethan, Maya, Diego, Hannah (notes)

Summary:
- Focus this week on landing the JIT kernel selector, stabilizing fused-attention kernel for GPT-like models, and iterating on KV cache eviction heuristics.
- Batching simulator results show a 9-12% net p95 latency reduction for mix-traffic when we enable dynamic headroom adjustment + kernel-level preemption.
- KV cache memory regression seen on long-prefix workloads; root cause narrowed to cache compaction edge case in new sharded allocator.

Highlights / Wins:
- Merged PR: kernel selector v2 (GH #842) -- ships runtime heuristics that choose between fused-attn and fallback kernels based on seq_len, model dims, and current batch occupancy. Initial canary shows 6-10% cost improvement for 4096-context workloads.
- Batching: dynamic-headroom mode enabled in dev cluster. Simulator + canary traffic shows improved throughput with negligible p99 increase for short requests.
- Added tracing spans to KV cache ops (put/get/evict) -- visible in Console traces for faster debugging.

Kernel work (owner: Ethan / Priya):
- JIT kernel selector: landed heuristics + lightweight profiler. Still need to add a fast-path for common 32k token seq distributions.
  - Perf: on A100 equivalent tests, fused-attn gives 8-11% lower token-ms for seq_len >= 2k on medium batch sizes.
  - TODO: add microbenchmark for seq_len=768/1024 to calibrate selector thresholds (Ethan).
- Fused-attn stabilization: fixed numeric edge case for padding masks (PR in review). Added additional fp16 numerics checks.
- Kernel fallback safety: introduced auto-rollback flag per-node to revert to fallback kernels on error spikes (configurable via Console).

KV cache (owner: Maya / Diego):
- Issue: memory growth on long-prefix (>50k tokens) workloads in dedicated canary. Root cause: during compaction, a sharded allocator misplaced a pointer resulting in retained slab references.
  - Steps taken: reverted allocator patch in canary, added regression test funnel for long-prefix retention.
  - Impact: observed 12-18% memory increase before revert; revert brought memory back to baseline.
- Eviction policy: experimenting with LRU+frequency hybrid. Early results: 4% lower miss-rate at similar memory footprint for web-chat workloads.
- Cache metrics: added per-shard hit/miss, tail-latency for cache-miss path. Visualized on Console dashboard (dashboard id linked).
- TODOs: finalize compaction fix and add end-to-end test (Maya). Add alert for cache growth > 20% over baseline for a node (Diego).

Batching (owner: Hannah / Priya):
- Dynamic headroom: new algorithm adjusts headroom based on recent arrival variance and model token-rate.
  - Simulator: ran on mixed traffic traces (prod-sampled week of 2026-05-24). With dynamic headroom + kernel-aware batching, we see: p95 down 9%, throughput up 6% on average.
  - Canary: enabled for 10% of hosted-api requests for small LLMs. Observed improved throughput and no customer-facing errors so far.
- Preemption: introduced soft-preemption where long-running batches yield to low-latency requests; reduces tail latency spikes in bursty scenarios.
- TODO: tune preemption thresholds to avoid throughput regressions for heavy embedding workloads (Hannah).

Operational notes / incidents: 
- Incident SRT-1678: KV cache compaction regression triggered elevated memory on 2 dedicated nodes. Root cause identified and mitigated by revert. Postmortem draft being started.
- Canary monitoring: keep an eye on p99 for models with >2048 context; kernel selector thresholds might be overly aggressive for some mid-sized models.

Blockers / Risks:
- Kernel selector: still missing microbench for 768/1024 seq lengths; selector may misroute a nontrivial fraction of requests for medium-context models. Risk: slight p99 regressions under certain traffic mixes.
- KV compaction: need to complete allocator patch with additional safety checks and a canary pass before rolling to Dedicated.
- Observability gaps: need better attribution of token-ms to kernel variants in the Console traces (work queued).

Next week / Plan:
- Land allocator fix + extended canary (Maya, Diego). Add regression suites for long-prefix traffic.
- Add microbench harness for medium seq_lens and update kernel selector thresholds (Ethan).
- Increase batching canary from 10% -> 25% if no regressions in 48h (Hannah).
- Finish postmortem for SRT-1678 and notify CS + Dedicated customers affected (Priya).

Action items (owners):
- Ethan: add microbench for seq_len=768/1024, run selector calibration by EOD 2026-06-21.
- Maya: complete compaction fix + unit tests, prepare extended canary (start 2026-06-18).
- Diego: add cache-growth alert and dashboard panel.
- Hannah: tune preemption thresholds; run throughput regression tests against embedding workloads.
- Priya: finalize postmortem draft and coordinate customer comms.

Meeting notes / standup snippets:
- 2026-06-15 standup: Diego reported memory spike on canary; Maya began revert; Ethan ramped down selector on 2 nodes.
- 2026-06-16 triage: decided to revert allocator patch and run extended traces.
- 2026-06-17 sync: agreed to prioritize microbench and canary expansion.

Open questions / discussion items:
- Should the kernel selector be conservative by default for Dedicated customers with very large context models? (suggestion: add per-customer override in config).
- How aggressive should preemption be for embedding throughput workloads vs. small-chat latency workloads? Need SLO-driven knob.

Notes to self / informal:
- Need to coordinate with Console team to expose kernel variant in trace attributes.
- Follow up with SRE on alert thresholds for memory growth; current default too high for long-prefix workloads.

Attachments / links: see linked_artifacts for GH/JIRA/Confluence.

Status: draft -- posting to shared_drive for visibility, will iterate after canary results next week.
